newsitem.title: SAUDI ARABIA: Saudi tells private firms to hire more locals.
newsitem.headline: Saudi tells private firms to hire more locals.

text.p: King Fahd of Saudi Arabia told private companies on Monday to employ more nationals in line with efforts to curb the high number of expatriates in the kingdom's workforce, the official Saudi news agency SPA said.
The king issued the directive during Monday's weekly council of ministers meeting which he chaired, it said.

The oil-rich kingdom's 1995-2000 development plan wants the private sector to find more jobs for its citizens to gradually curb reliance on millions of expatriates who help run the Saudi Arabian economy.
It set a target of creating 659,000 jobs for Saudis by the turn of the century. Less than seven percent of the private sector workers are Saudis.

"...King Fahd stressed the goals which had to be achieved (to realise the five-year plan), including rationalising the growth of the expatriate workforce in all sectors," Information Minister Fouad bin Abdul-Salam bin Mohammad Farsi told SPA.

"Other goals included finding more job opportunities to Saudi newcomers to the labour market, especially in the private sector and increasing employment opportunities for Saudi women in jobs allowed by the Islamic sharia...."

King Fahd also stressed the need to develop statistical data on the labour market and to give more attention to education and training of Saudis to enable them fill jobs held by foreigners, Farsi added.
Saudi Arabia's other Gulf Arab allies have launched similar plans to find more jobs for their citizens.
While there are no official unemployment figures in Saudi Arabia, analysts say the jobless rate is above 10 percent and rising.
The foreigners - mostly from the Indian subcontinent, southeast Asia, Egypt and other Arab countries - comprise about one third of the kingdom's population of 18 million.
